newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees Aug auction of Yauricocha, oil terminals.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees Aug auction of Yauricocha, oil terminals.

text.p: Peru plans to auction in August its Yauricocha mine and eight oil terminal concessions as part of a new schedule for its privatization plan, COPRI, the government body overseeing the program, said Tuesday.
The announcement marks a step forward for the program as both privatizations suffered setbacks last year.
The Yauricocha sale was postponed after the government failed to attract potential buyers for the unit despite lowering the minimum bid price 15 percent to $8.5 million.

COPRI did not announce the new base price for the polymetallic mine, which lies 220 miles (350 km) southeast of Lima and has proven and probable reserves of 2.8 million tonnes and potential reserves of six million tonnes.
In the oil sector, offering concessions marks a change in government strategy, which had previously passed state firm Petroperu's non-exploration oil assets into the private sector with direct sales.
Last November, the government put on hold its oil privatization program after the sale of a 60 percent stake in its La Pampilla refinery raised public fears of gasoline price hikes.
COPRI's new schedule sets out plans to place in private hands over the next six months up to 20 state assets in the oil, mining, electricity and fishing sectors.
The government's next major privatization is the planned July sale of Mahr Tunel -- two mining production units on the slate as a single asset.
